original_question: Let H : Top0 -> Set be an irreducible subset system, let X be a T0 space, and let Y be a super H-sober space. If Top0(X, Y) is equipped with the topology of pointwise convergence, must this function space Top0(X, Y) be super H-sober?
target_in_paper: Section 1, Problem 2: the paper’s restatement of Xu’s question about whether pointwise-convergence function spaces with super H-sober codomain remain super H-sober.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s intended target. It correctly uses an irreducible subset system H (the paper’s standard term is “R-subset system”), a T0 space X, a super H-sober space Y, the function space Top0(X,Y), and the topology of pointwise convergence, and it asks exactly the right closure question. It also correctly does not impose any extra hypothesis such as property M on H, which is the point of the paper’s reformulation of the problem.
missing_details: State explicitly that H: Top0 -> Set is an R-subset system, meaning H(Z) is a family of irreducible subsets of Z for every T0 space Z.
Define Top0(X,Y) as the set of all continuous maps f: X -> Y.
Specify that the topology of pointwise convergence is the subspace topology inherited from the product space Y^X.
Define “super H-sober” at least parenthetically, as meaning that the Smyth power space PS(Y) is H-sober.
Make the quantifiers explicit: the question is for every R-subset system H, every T0 space X, and every super H-sober space Y.
refined_question: Let H: Top0 -> Set be an R-subset system, i.e. H(Z) is a family of irreducible subsets of each T0 space Z. For a T0 space X and a super H-sober space Y (meaning that the Smyth power space PS(Y) is H-sober), let Top0(X,Y) denote the set of all continuous maps f: X -> Y, endowed with the topology of pointwise convergence, equivalently the subspace topology inherited from the product Y^X. Must Top0(X,Y) be super H-sober?
justification: The draft matches the paper’s Problem 2 essentially verbatim. The nearby context needed to make it stand-alone is: the paper’s standard terminology “R-subset system”; the definition of super H-sober via the Smyth power space; and the intended meaning of the pointwise-convergence topology on Top0(X,Y) as the relative product topology. The paper’s later discussion shows why this exact formulation, without any added property-M hypothesis, is the right one: Proposition 5.3 proves that every R-subset system automatically has property M, and then the paper states that Problem 2 follows from Xu’s earlier Theorem 6.20 together with that proposition.
